draw_lifecycle.kill_switch: config('lottery.automation.enabled') -- when false the task is NOT registered at all, rather than registered and returning early. The subcommands carry the same guard, so a manual run is also refused without --force.
draw_lifecycle.deliberately_excluded: lottery:publish-result. Publication is a human-approved step by design, documented in TickCommand::STEPS. This is correct and was left alone.

unscheduled_console_commands.assessment: Most declared commands are correctly manual: operator tools (glo:freeze-ticket, glo:freeze-case, glo:breaker, glo:stress-harness), one-shot rebuilds (grades:rebuild-snapshots) and ad-hoc imports. The phase-7 open list mixed three different things together - lanes that were already scheduled, read-only monitoring lanes that genuinely had no producer, and draw-scoped operator actions that cannot have one. Cluster #46 separated them: the monitoring lanes are scheduled, the already-scheduled ones are recorded as such, and the operator actions stay open with the reason each one cannot be a cron entry.
open_findings: glo:notify-saved-tickets -- saved-ticket holders are never told their number came up. Kept open on purpose: the command requires --draw= and refuses to run without it, so a cron entry would fail on every tick. What is missing is a producer that picks the draws to notify, and inventing that selection rule means deciding which customers get told, on a schedule, without a spec.

glo:process-frozen-winners -- frozen winners are never released. Kept open: it takes an actor (resolveActor) and holds payouts, which is a money decision, not a cadence. --dry-run exists, so the honest next step is reporting what it would hold, not automating the release.

glo:reconcile-sales -- sales reconciliation never runs per draw. Kept open: requires --draw= and an authenticated actor holding RECONCILE_LEDGER or PROCESS_SETTLEMENTS (measured: it exits non-zero with '--draw= is required.' when run bare), which makes it an operator action by construction.
unscheduled_console_commands.count_note: 29 was measured as the number of declared commands with no producer during phase 7. It is left as the phase-7 number rather than re-derived, because the sentence it belongs to is a history of that phase; the current state is the three blocks below, and each of them is verified by a test that runs today.

ops:evaluate-alerts.why_this_cadence: OperationalAlertService::DEFAULT_THROTTLE_SECONDS is 900; a lane slower than its own cooldown can spend a whole window between looks.

queue:health --json.why_this_cadence: The command's own --json option text says the JSON form exists for automated monitoring. A schedule entry is that automation; the exit code is the report.

glo:provider-health --json.why_this_cadence: It reports a circuit breaker counted over config('glo.sources.breaker.window_seconds'), 300 by default, so a report older than that window describes a source that may have already recovered.

contact:delivery-health.why_this_cadence: It reports whether forwarding is configured: a configuration fact that changes on deploy, not a live queue. Placed after contact:purge at 03:40 so one reading covers the contact lane.

chat:health --json.why_this_cadence: Also gated on chat.enabled: a health report for a feature that is switched off is noise that reads like a finding.

findings_that_were_stale.now: finance:reconcile has had a schedule entry since the ledger-reconciliation cluster, gated on finance.ledger.auto_reconcile and cadenced from finance.ledger.reconciliation_interval through ReconciliationCadence. What is true is narrower and worth keeping: the shipped .env template sets FINANCE_LEDGER_AUTO_RECONCILE=false while config/finance.php defaults it to true, so an install that copies the template does leave the control off.
findings_that_were_stale.verification: php artisan schedule:list shows the entry when the flag is on; bootstrap/app.php gates it on ReconciliationCadence::isAutoReconcileEnabled(config('finance.ledger.auto_reconcile', false)); tests/Feature/Console/LedgerReconciliationScheduleTest.php pins both halves.

findings_that_were_stale.was: glo:expire-freezes -- a freeze that never expires holds a winner's prize indefinitely, unscheduled
findings_that_were_stale.now: Scheduled hourly since the freeze-expiry cluster (->hourly(), withoutOverlapping(10), storage/logs/glo-freeze-expiry.log). The finding was written before that wiring and was left standing in the open list.
findings_that_were_stale.verification: bootstrap/app.php contains the entry; ScheduledClockProducersTest asserts it exists exactly once with the house safety flags.

findings_that_were_stale.was: contact:purge / contact:delivery-health -- contact retention and delivery health never run
findings_that_were_stale.now: Half of it was stale and half of it was real until this cluster: contact:purge has been scheduled daily since the retention cluster, and contact:delivery-health is scheduled now (dailyAt 03:45, flag OPS_LANE_DELIVERY_HEALTH).
findings_that_were_stale.verification: pattern count of $schedule->command entries in bootstrap/app.php, asserted by OperationalLaneTruthTest.

findings_that_were_stale.was: ops:evaluate-alerts / ops:metrics-export -- the observability lane produces nothing
findings_that_were_stale.now: ops:evaluate-alerts is scheduled every five minutes. ops:metrics-export stays unscheduled on purpose: its output is a pull target served over HTTP by the route named metrics, and writing the same text into a log file on a timer would produce a file no scraper reads.
findings_that_were_stale.verification: ScheduledClockProducersTest::test_every_exemption_cites_a_fact_that_still_holds resolves both halves live: the route must exist and the lane must be scheduled.

result_import_finding.finding: No result importer is scheduled on any lane (glo, national, weekly, bingo, pcso). The lifecycle advances a draw to results-pending and it stays there forever unless an operator runs an import by hand.
result_import_finding.second_finding: Every lane importer declared {--provider=fixture} as its DEFAULT option value. A no-argument run -- exactly what a cron entry or a hurried operator would do -- would have imported fabricated results into a real draw.
result_import_finding.fix_applied: The default was changed to official on all four lane importers (ImportNationalLotteryResults, ImportWeeklyLotteryResults, ImportBingoLotteryResults, ImportPcsoLotteryResults). A run with no provider now targets the official source and fails closed if it is unreachable, instead of silently fabricating a result.
result_import_finding.still_open: The importers remain unscheduled. Scheduling them requires each lane's official provider endpoint and credentials, which are not present in this environment, so a schedule entry here would be cargo cult.

definition_sites_are_the_two_named_files.statement: The scheduler is defined in exactly the two places this artifact lists; a third would mean the inventory is no longer the map.

entries_at_least.statement: At least 34 entries, counted as definitions in the two sites (29 through phase 7, plus the five operational lanes added in cluster #46).

result_importers_remain_unscheduled.statement: The critical open finding of phase 7 is still open: no :import command appears in either definition site, so results still never arrive by themselves.

operational_lanes_are_scheduled.statement: All five read-only operational lanes appear as schedule entries in bootstrap/app.php.

each_lane_is_switched_by_a_flag_it_owns.statement: Every lane entry is guarded by its own config('ops.lanes.*') read, so an operator can switch one off without editing the scheduler.

lane_flags_reach_the_operator.statement: Each of the five lane flags appears in the shipped .env template as a commented default, so the config value (on) applies until an operator says otherwise.

verification.pattern_note: No leading # and no line anchor: the gate's re() helper treats a pattern beginning with # as already delimited, and compiles bare patterns with the i flag only, so ^ would look at the start of the file rather than the start of each line.

the_lane_claims_are_gated_not_asserted.statement: The read-only, cadence and exemption claims in this artifact are checked by a test file that runs the commands, rather than being believed from this JSON.
